notes.text:
Independent mathematical verdict on actual author n1: PASS.

Put q=gamma+u with |u|<=C, and let F(x) be the infimum of finite legal printed PCC-tree costs rooted at x. Every internal node keeps its own finite rational witnessing structure and tau<=sigma_i incidence, rational children, real nonnegative weights summing to one, and actual parent barycenter. Nonminimal center faces, repeated occurrences and an unsplit real root are allowed. Zero-weight subtrees can be deleted with the same witness. No common refinement preserving a node's incidence is presumed, and a terminal barycenter alone is insufficient.

Repeated Jensen for the actual PC reference gives every tree cost >=gamma(x)-C. The single-leaf tree gives F(x)<=q(x). Every original finite-valued raw PC competitor f<=q is bounded above by every tree cost through finite repeated Jensen. This includes irrational downward spikes, discontinuity, and competitors with upper-only growth and no lower bound. Consequently E_gamma(u)<=F.

For any legal split, choose finitely many child trees within eta of their finite infima and graft them. Since the split weights sum to one, the total error is at most eta. Letting eta decrease gives F(x)<=sum alpha_i F(x_i), for every permitted witnessing structure. F is therefore finite-valued printed PC. Its sandwich supplies the original growth upper bound, so F itself is an original competitor. Hence F=E_gamma(u), before continuity, density or MA.

Only afterward does qualified R230 apply: the support is finite rational, positive and balanced at every facet; gamma is the actual continuous PC reference; u is bounded continuous. It supplies continuity of the actual endpoint and real-endpoint PCC inequalities, without asserting continuity of every raw competitor. Each real-endpoint tree bounds this continuous endpoint from above, while printed trees already have its exact infimum.

The reference excess telescopes exactly as sum_internal pi_b(sum_i alpha_bi gamma(x_bi)-gamma(x_b)); each term is nonnegative. Positive actual recession slopes and finite point/ray representations give gamma(x)>=a||x||-b for some a>0. Nonzero lineality in a gamma-affine cell is impossible. Thus H=gamma+c>=0 can be chosen proper.

For an eta-optimal tree, its terminal probability nu satisfies integral H dnu<=H(x)+2C+eta. Evaluating the SAME legal tree with another obstacle v gives, after reversing u,v and letting eta decrease,
|E_gamma(u)(x)-E_gamma(v)(x)|<=sup_{H<=R}|u-v|+2C(H(x)+2C)/R.
This proves bounded local-uniform obstacle-to-envelope convergence. The terminal probability is a cost distribution, not MA; intermediate tree infima or Bellman iterates receive no measure.
